This application under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. has been filed seeking following relief(s):-
relief(s):
"It is, therefore, most humbly prayed that this Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to summon the entire record of criminal proceeding quash the First Information Report Report (F.I.R.) No.0101/2022 lodged on 17/03/2022 wherein offence U/s 498-A 498 A of I.P.C. and U/s 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act against the petitioner and the entire criminal proceedings pending before the J.M.F.C. Narmadapuram,
Distt.Narmadapuram in RCT No.1588/2022 may please be quashed to secure the ends of justice." 
2. It is fairly conceded by counsel for the applicants applicant that the charges have already been framed.

5. Applicant No.1 is the husband, applicant No.2 is the father father-in-law and applicant No.3 is the mother-in-law mother law of respondent No.2. 
6. According to the applicants, the first marriage of applicant No.1 with one Monika Singh ended in a mutual divorce. The said fact was within the knowledge of respondent No.2 and her parents. In paragraph 4 of the application, it has been submitted by the applicants that since respondent No.2 is also the resident of Itarsi, therefore the aforesaid fact was in the knowledge of respondent No.2 and her parents. The marriage of applicant No.1 and respondent No.2 was solemnized on 06/12/2020. 
After few weeks of marriage, applicant No.1 noticed that respondent No.2 is in habit of eating Gutka. 
Since applicant No.1 and applicant No.3 were objecting to the consumption of Gutka,, therefore respondent No.22 used to argue with them pleading that no harm would be caused to them. After some time, respondent No.2 started misbehaving with the parents of the applicant No.1 as she was not interested to take up the household responsibilities. She was unhappy with the the interferences by elders of the house. After six months of marriage, respondent No.2 left the house of applicants applicant and went to her parental home. Applicant No.1 informed the Police with regard to the behavior and tried to get the matter resolved by submitting submit an application to In-charge,
charge, Police Station Itarsi on 12/05/2021. The applicants tried their best to resolve the dispute by making an effort to realize the respondent No.2 about her family responsibilities but respondent No.2 was not ready to adjust erself. Accordingly, an application before Parivar Paramarsh Kendra herself. 
Itarsi was submitted on 21/06/2021. Notices were issued to respondent No.2. The statements of both the parties were recorded. 
recorded. However, on NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:40688 JBP:40688 24/02/2022 she filed an application before Parivar Paramarsh Kendra Sohagpur, District Narmadapuram by leveling false allegations against the applicants and wanted to proceed legally against them. Again notices were issued to the applicants but the matter again ended without any solution. Accordingly, respondent res No.2 lodged the FIR No.101/2022 at Police Station Babai,
District Hoshangabad for offence under Sections 498-A, A, 294, 506 of IPC and under Sections 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act. Applicants have also made complaints complaint to Superintendent of Police and other her senior police officers but they did not get any respite and ultimately, the Police filed a charge-sheet sheet and charges under Sections 498-A A of IPC and under Sections 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act were framed by JMFC Narmadapuram in Criminal Case No.1588/20 No.1588/2022.

2 7. It is submitted that the allegations made in the FIR are false, baseless and are general and omnibus in nature. The same are not sufficient to prosecute the applicants. It is further submitted by counsel for the applicants that the statement of respondent respondent No.2 was recorded in the Parivar Paramarsh Kendra in which it was stated by her that the applicants No.2 and 3 should not interfere in the family affairs of applicant No.1 and respondent No.2. It was only alleged that applicant No.1 and applicant No.3 constantly interferes in the household works. Thus, it is submitted that the allegations made in the FIR are false. 
8. Per contra, application is vehemently opposed by counsel for the State. 
9. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
10. As already pointed out, applicants applicants have not clarified the date on which charges were framed. Even the order framing charge has not been filed and there is no averment as to whether charges were ever NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:40688 JBP:40688 challenged by the applicants applicant before Revisional Court or not. Even counsel for applicants could not clarify that how this application under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. would be maintainable which has been filed after the charges were framed. 
11. As per the FIR, marriage took place on 06/12/202 06/12/2020. According to the complainant her parents had given household articles and cash Rs.6,50,000/- for purchasing Swift car. For one month, she was kept properlyy in her matrimonial house. Thereafter applicants started demanding Rupees Five Lakhs and on account accoun of non-fulfillment fulfillment of said demand, they started harassing her physically and mentally mentally. Her husband used to beat her and was alleging that unless and until she brings an additional amount, she will be beaten and one day she will be killed. However, she was was tolerating the atrocities. The cruelty which was being committed by the applicants was narrated by the complainant to her parents, who also tried to convince her that with passage of time, the things would improve but they are not in a position to fulfil fulfill the demand of the applicants. In the meanwhile, her parents also tried to convince and pursue the applicants but things did not improve. The husband of respondent No.2 is running a private medical shop, whereas applicant No.2 is working as Compounder in Primary Health Centre Matkuli. For fulfillment of their demands, they were continuously harassing her physically and mentally. On 2 or 3 occasions, her parents came to Itarsi to take her back but they were turned out of the house by the applicants. About six ix months back, her husband has left her at parental house with a threat that unless and until until she brings the amount, she sh should not come back to her matrimonial house. Since respondent No.2 was fed up with the cruelty meted out to her, therefore she made a complaint to One Stop NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:40688 JBP:40688 Centre Hoshangabad and Parivar Paramarsh Kendra, Sohagpu Sohagpur but she also did not get any relief from any of the said institution and she was suggested that she should take the help of Police Station and Court Court. 
After fter the marriage, marriage she came to know that the applicant No.1 was married to one Monika Singh. It was also alleged that applicants must have misbehaved with Monika Singh compelling her to take divorce. On 09/03/2022 at about 02:00 PM, applicant No.1 came to her Manoj Nayak vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194749341/
3 parental home in village llage Keerpura and abused her and her parents and threatened that unless and until the amount is arranged, she should not be sent to her matrimonial house. In case if any report is lodged, then they would be killed. Accordingly, the FIR was lodged. 
12. From thee various complaints made by the applicant No.1 to the different Police Stations, it is clear that the relation relationships of the applicants with respondent No.1 were w not cordial. 
13. Applicants have also filed a copy of the proceedings of Parivar Paramarsh Kendra Sohagpur S in which respondent No.2 had made a statement that "although although she is willing to stay with applicant No.1 but applicant No.1 is in habit of assaulting her. Applicants are also treating her with cruelty on account of demand of Rupees Five Lakhs. It wa was further alleged that in case if applicant No.1 do not assault her and do not demand dowry, then she is ready to reside with him him". "However, applicant No.1 had stated that he is not ready to keep respondent No.2 with him because she consumes Gutka and use filthy language. He further stated that he has already given Rs.4,50,000/-". 
14. Thus it is clear that two different sets of allegations were made by the parties before Parivar Paramarsh Kendra Itarsi and Parivar Paramarsh Kendra Sohagpur. 
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:40688 JBP:40688 15. It is well established established principle of law that this Court while exercising power under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. cannot consider the correctness, reliability and credibility of the allegations made by the parties. This Court cannot conduct a mini trial. Whether the allegations which were made before Parivar Paramarsh Kendra Itarsi are correct or the allegations which were made before Parivar Paramarsh Kendra Sohagpur are correct and whether the allegations which have been made by respondent No.2 are correct, cannot be adjudicated adjudicated by this Court and the same can be adjudicated by the Trial Court only after recording the evidence of the parties. The applicants would get full opportunity to cross-examine examine the respondent No.2 to get the things clarified. 
16. The Supreme Court in the case of o Taramani Parakh Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh and Others reported in (2015) 11 SCC 260 has held as under:-
"12. In Kailash Chandra Agrawal v. State of U.P. (2014) 16 SCC 551, 551, it was observed (SCC p. 553, paras 8-9):
"8.. We have gone through the FIR and the criminal complaint. In the FIR, the appellants have not been named and in the criminal complaint they have been named without attributing any specific role to them. The relationship of the appellants with the husband of the complainant is distant. In Kans Raj v. State of Punjab (2000) 5 SCC 207 : 2000 SCC (Cri) 935 : (2000) 3 SCR 662]it was observed (SCC p. 217, para 5):
"5.. ... A tendency has, however, developed for roping in all relations of the in in- Manoj Nayak vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194749341/
4 laws of the deceased wives in the matters of dowry deaths deaths which, if not discouraged, is likely to affect the case of the prosecution even against the real culprits. In their NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:40688 JBP:40688 overenthusiasm and anxiety to seek conviction for maximum people, the parents of the deceased have been found to be making efforts for involving involving other relations which ultimately weaken the case of the prosecution even against the real accused as appears to have happened in the instant case." 
The Court has, thus, to be careful in summoning distant relatives without there being specific material. 
material. Only the husband, his parents or at best close family members may be expected to demand dowry or to harass the wife but not distant relations, unless there is tangible material to support allegations made against such distant relations. Mere naming of of distant relations is not enough to summon them in the absence of any specific role and material to support such role. 
9.. The parameters for quashing proceedings in a criminal complaint are well known. If there are triable issues, the Court is not expected expected to go into the veracity of the rival versions but where on the face of it, the criminal proceedings are abuse of Court's process, quashing jurisdiction can be exercised. Reference may be made to K. Ramakrishna v. State of Bihar,, (2000) 8 SCC 547 :
2001 SCC S (Cri) 27, Pepsi Foods Ltd. v. Judicial Magistrate, (1998) 5 SCC 749 : 1998 SCC (Cri)
Magistrate, 1400, State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal,, 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335 : 1992 SCC (Cri) 426 : AIR 1992 SC 604 and Asmathunnisa v. State of A.P.,, (2011) 11 SCC 259 : (2011) 3 SCC (Cri) ( 159."
13. In the present case, the complaint is as follows:
"Sir, it is submitted that I was married on 18 18-11- 2009 with Sidharath Parakh s/o Manak Chand Parakh r/o Sarafa Bazar in front of Radha Krishna Market, Gwalior according to the Hindu rites and customs. In the marriage my father had given gold and silver ornaments, cash amount and household NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-JBP:40688 JBP:40688 goods according to his capacity. After the marriage when I went to my matrimonial home, I was treated nicely by the members of the family. When on the second occasion I went to my matrimonial home, my husband, father-in-law father law and mother mother-in- law started harassing me for not bringing the dowry and started saying that I should bring from my father 25-30 25 30 tolas of gold and Rs 2,00,000 in cash and only then they would keep me in the house otherwise not. On account of this my husband also used to beat me and my father- father-in-law and my mother-in-law mother law used to torture me by giving the taunts. In this connection I used to tell my father Kundanmal Oswal, my mother Smt Prem Lata Oswal, swal, uncle Ashok Rai Sharma and uncle Ved Prakash Mishra from time to time. On 22-4- 2010 the members of the family of my matrimonial home Manoj Nayak vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194749341/
5 forcibly sent me to the house of my parents in Ganj Basoda along with my brother Deepak. They snatched my clothes and ornaments and kept with them. Since then till today my husband has been harassing me on the telephone and has not come to take me back. Being compelled, I have been moving this application before you. Sir, it is prayed that action be taken against husband Sidharath Parakh, my father father-in- law Manak Chand Parakh and my mother-mother-in-law Smt Indira Parakh for torturing me on account of demanding dowry. 
14. From a reading of the complaint, it cannot be held that even if the allegations are taken as proved no case is made out. There are allegations against Respondent 2 and his parents for harassing the complainant which forced her to leave the matrimonial home. Even now she continues to be separated from the matrimonial home as she apprehends lack of security and safety safety and proper environment in the matrimonial home. The question whether the appellant has in fact been harassed and treated with cruelty is a matter of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:40688 JBP:40688 trial but at this stage, it cannot be said that no case is made out. Thus, quashing of proceedings before the trial is not permissible."
permissible. 
17. Although the charge-sheet charge sheet has already been filed and charges have been framed but still the applicants have not filed the complete charge-sheet sheet to point out the allegations made by respondent No.2 and other witnesses in their statements under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. 
18 . It is well established principle of law that the FIR is not an encyclopedia. 
19. Accordingly, in absence of complete charge-sheet charge sheet as well as in view of limited scope of jurisdiction under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., this Court is of considered opinion that the charge-sheet charge sheet filed against the applicants cannot be quashed. 
20. For the reasons mentioned above, application fails and is hereby dismissed.
